general_conventions: M1 = method mark; A marks dependent on it cannot be scored unless the M mark is earned. A1 = accuracy/answer mark, often awarded for a correct final answer which then implies earlier C marks.
C1 = compensatory (method) mark that can be awarded for correct working even if the final answer is wrong; a correct final answer normally earns all C marks.
B1 = independent mark, not dependent on other marks.
A0 on a show-that line means the given value earns no credit by itself; the mark is for the working shown.

ECF (error carried forward): later numerical parts can earn full credit if consistent with an earlier wrong answer; ECF is allowed after arithmetic (AE), transcription (TE) and power-of-ten (POT) errors but not after wrong physics/equation (XP).
POT: power-of-ten error, usually from SI prefix conversion; the mark where it happens is lost, then ECF applies.
TE: wrong copying of data from question, graph, booklet or earlier answer; lose that mark only, then ECF.
XP: using an incorrect equation counts as wrong physics even if it gives the right number.
SF: giving more significant figures than justified is not penalised; too few sig figs is handled within individual mark points and penalised only once in the paper.
CON: contradictory statements in one answer score no mark. BOD = benefit of the doubt.

Conventions: '/' separates alternative acceptable answers; Reject/Not = not creditworthy; Ignore = irrelevant; Allow = acceptable; words in brackets are not essential; underlined words must appear; AW = alternative wording; ORA = or reverse argument.

Level of Response (6-mark, asterisked) questions are marked holistically: decide the level from the science and the quality of reasoning, then the higher/lower mark within the level by communication. L1 = 1-2, L2 = 3-4, L3 = 5-6 marks; L1^/L2^/L3^ annotate the lower mark in each level.

LoR communication strands: L3 needs a well-developed line of reasoning, clear and logically structured, relevant and substantiated; L2 a line of reasoning with some structure, mostly relevant, supported by some evidence; L1 basic, unstructured information with limited evidence; 0 = nothing worthy of credit.
Alternative correct approaches and unexpected methods must be credited fairly.

MACB categorisation: B marks must be specifically seen; M marks must be seen and gate dependent A marks; C marks can be implied by later correct working (e.g. a correct substitution implies knowledge of the equation); A marks depend on an M mark or allow C marks to be scored.
Significant figures rule: if data are given to 2 s.f., answers to 2 or more s.f. are allowed; fewer than 2 s.f. is penalised once only in the whole paper unless additional guidance says otherwise.
For substitution into an equation any rearranged subject is allowed unless guidance says otherwise.
Crossed-out work is not marked if a clear alternative is given; contradictory responses score nothing even if one part is correct.
List questions: only the required number of responses are marked, left to right then line by line; extra responses hedging bets gain no credit.
NR is used when nothing is written; 0 is given for written work not worthy of credit (including copying the question).

LoR marking (2025 wording): start at the highest level and work down to the level matching the answer; within the level, borderline answers get the bottom mark, answers that consistently meet the criteria get the top mark, with intermediate cases (just enough / slight inconsistency) placed accordingly.
Levels of response questions on this paper are 4(b) and 8.

questions.context: Train's acceleration during braking from simplified v-t graph.
allow_reject_ignore: Allow other gradient values that round to 0.45 in magnitude
pitfalls: Including the thinking time (0-8 s) in Δt

questions.subtopic: stopping distance from area under v-t
questions.context: Total stopping distance from t = 0 using graph.
marking_points: C1: any correct area, e.g. ½(8 + 128) × 54, 8 × 54 or ½ × 120 × 54

questions.context: Why simplified graph is not the train's real motion.
questions.answer: Deceleration not constant and would not change suddenly (gradual onset); braking/drag forces vary with speed
marking_points: B1 (any two): acceleration not constant / line would be curved
B1: acceleration would not change suddenly - builds up/decreases gradually
B1: to avoid passengers feeling sudden forces
B1: brakes cannot apply maximum force instantly / friction and air resistance change with speed
pitfalls: Generic 'air resistance' without linking to changing deceleration

questions.subtopic: choice of fixed resistor in sensor
questions.context: Why 120 kΩ fixed resistor is unsuitable for 0-100 °C sensing.
questions.answer: Almost all p.d. across 120 kΩ; voltmeter barely changes (~4.7-4.8 V)

questions.context: One similarity and one difference between e.m.f. and p.d.
questions.answer: Both energy per unit charge; e.m.f. converts other forms to electrical, p.d. electrical to other forms
marking_points: B1: similarity - both work done (energy transferred) per unit charge
B1: difference - e.m.f. transfers chemical/other energy to electrical (work done on charges) AND p.d. transfers electrical to heat/other (work done by charges)
allow_reject_ignore: Allow joule per coulomb; both parts of difference needed
pitfalls: Giving only half of the difference

questions.context: Describe safe potentiometer experiment, with diagram, to compare e.m.f.s of two cells.
questions.answer: Find balance lengths lA, lB (and l0 for 2.2 V reference); E_A/E_B = lA/lB
marking_points: L3 (5-6): clear diagram and detailed method to compare/measure e.m.f.s of A and B using potentiometer with relevant analysis
L2 (3-4): diagram and some method with relevant analysis; OR good method with analysis; OR clear diagram with limited method
L1 (1-2): limited method to compare A and B
Indicative (diagram): driver battery across potentiometer wire; cell A or B connected with galvanometer/meter; workable circuit

Indicative (method): vary contact position; find balance (null) point; detail of finding balance e.g. reduce meter sensitivity; measure balance length l0 (known e.m.f.), lA and lB; E_A = (lA/l0) × 2.2, E_B = (lB/l0) × 2.2
Indicative (alternative): measure I and V for different lengths; graph V vs I; E = y-intercept
Indicative (safety): switch off between readings to avoid heating wire; resistor to limit current
pitfalls: Cells connected opposing incorrectly (no balance possible)

questions.subtopic: Planck constant from LEDs with uncertainty
questions.context: Describe measuring LED striking p.d. accurately; use V vs f graph to find h, K and % uncertainty in h.
questions.answer: gradient ≈ 2.4 × 10^-15 V s = h/e so h ≈ 3.8 × 10^-34 J s; intercept ≈ -0.97 V gives K ≈ 1.55 × 10^-19 J
marking_points: L3 (5-6): clear description of measuring V, h and K determined and percentage uncertainty in h determined correctly
L2 (3-4): limited description of V with detailed attempt at h and K or h and % uncertainty; OR clear description with limited attempt at those
L1 (1-2): limited description of V measurement OR limited attempt at h, K or % uncertainty

Indicative (measurement): voltmeter across LED; reduce variable resistance until LED just lights; tube to shield from background light; darken room; repeat by increasing resistance until LED just goes off

Indicative (analysis): gradient = h/e and y-intercept = -K/e; h = gradient × 1.6 × 10^-19; gradient ≈ 2.4 × 10^-15 V s; h ≈ 3.8 × 10^-34 J s; intercept ≈ -0.97 V; K ≈ 1.55 × 10^-19 J; correct powers of ten and units; worst acceptable line, its gradient, absolute and % uncertainty in gradient; % uncertainty in h = % uncertainty in gradient
pitfalls: Reading intercept at x = 2.0 rather than extrapolating to f = 0
